messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High tail latency detected for /v1/generate in eu-west2 -> p99 spikes to 1.2s, streaming stalls increasing. Severity: P2. Auto-page sent to #incidents and on-call.
oncall-amber: saw the page, joining. any initial notes? :wave:
lee: seeing p95 ~220ms (normal ~120ms), p99 ~1.2s. Streaming stall metric shows increased stall-rate on connections routed cross-AZ.
sam: same. top customer errors are timeouts on long-lived streaming connections (chunk delays). Any recent infra deploys?
maria: no deployments in serving runtime in the last 30m. I do see a routing policy change rolled out to eu-west2 yesterday that adjusted egress routing for a subset of prod pools to prefer cross-AZ NAT for cost optimization.
lee: that could be it. graphs show spike coincident with the rollout (approx 1865004100).
infra-bot: recent change: route-policy-eu-west2 v3.4 -> applied to pool-prod-4 at 1864999000 by infra-ops.
jordan: customer impact: 4 customers with streaming heavy usage have visible stalls; approx 1.8% of overall requests show >500ms token gaps. No full outages.
oncall-amber: ok triage plan: 1) confirm packet loss / TLS handshake retries cross-zone 2) rollback route-policy to prior when safe 3) apply short-term mitigation (pin streams to same AZ or force local NAT) 4) keep customers updated.
sam: running tcpdump on one of the affected nodes now, capturing TLS handshake retransmits. Paste of sample: ```17:22:01.123456 IP a.b.c.d.443 > x.y.z.w.52000: Flags [P.], seq 1:143, ack 1, win 229, length 142
17:22:01.223789 IP x.y.z.w.52000 > a.b.c.d.443: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0, length 0```
lee: also running kpacketcat across AZ boundary showing increased retransmits and occasional RTOs.
maria: checked NAT gateway metrics: ephemeral port saturation on nat-gw-eu-west2-b peaking; port exhaustion counters incrementing when streaming sessions pooled to that gateway.
infra-bot: nat-gw-eu-west2-b ephemeral_ports_used=62498/65535, conn_rate spike at 18k/s.
jordan: that explains the R resets. long-lived streaming clients hold ports, cross-AZ routing funnels too many streams through same nat-gw causing reuse/exhaustion.
oncall-amber: mitigation step A: revert route-policy-eu-west2 to v3.3 to restore local egress preference. infra, can you roll that back now?
maria: starting rollback now, will run canary on pool-prod-1 then expand. ETA 4m.
sam: while rollback runs, can we add a temporary policy to pin streaming sessions by tag to same AZ? config snippet: ```policies:
  - name: pin-stream-az
    match: session.tags.streaming==true
    action: prefer_local_az_egress```
lee: good idea. product-ops, any concerns exposing that rule quickly?
product-ops: fine with emergency rule for 1 hour, notify customers after.
maria: rollback canary green on pool-prod-1, expanding to remaining pools. pushing full revert now.
infra-bot: route-policy-eu-west2 now at v3.3 on pool-prod-1/2/3/4. change completed at 1865004820.
oncall-amber: monitoring metrics for improvement. anyone seeing p99 drop?
sam: p99 down to 480ms in next 2m. streaming stall-rate down ~60%.
lee: TLS handshake retries rate decreased ~70% and nat-gw saturation counters dropping.
jordan: still seeing some residual stalls for customers that had long-lived sessions started during the storm. might need session-level reconnects.
oncall-amber: action item: trigger graceful reconnect for affected dedicated pools to migrate sessions to new egress path. Sam/Lee to coordinate.
sam: running a rolling reconnect for pool-prod-4. command: ```for node in $(list-nodes pool-prod-4); do curl -X POST http://$node/admin/reconnect?grace=30; done```
lee: logs show reconnects succeeding, downstream clients reconnecting within 15s mostly.
infra-bot: nat-gw-eu-west2-b ephemeral_ports_used=43210/65535 after mitigations.
maria: as further mitigation, I've opened a ticket to increase ephemeral port range and autoscale nat-gw capacity for eu-west2 cluster.
oncall-amber: customer comms: Jordan, can you prepare short note for the four impacted customers describing cause (egress route change -> nat port saturation -> TLS resets -> streaming stalls) and actions taken? Emphasize no data loss and restores in X mins.
jordan: drafting now, will share for review.
product-ops: queued a post-incident review on calendar for tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Please attach metric graphs and policy diff.
oncall-amber: handoff: I'm paging off in 30m. Lee will be primary until tomorrow morning. Lee, take over and own postmortem.
lee: taking handoff. current status: latency improved, streaming stalls reduced, nat gw under threshold. next steps: collect traces, collect tcpdumps from affected nodes, coordinate port range change with infra, write postmortem.
oncall-amber: thanks team. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved; will set incident_status=mitigated. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: mitigated at 1865005600. oncall: lee.
lee: filing short incident stub in #incidents later with links to dashboards.
jordan: shared customer note with legal and support; sending to customers in 15m.
product-ops: adding runbook step to vet egress route rollouts against nat gw saturation and long-lived stream heuristics.
lee: agreed. capturing the config diff here for postmortem: ```- prefer_cross_az_egress: true
+ prefer_local_az_egress: true```
oncall-amber: great work everyone. we should be ready to close after postmortem. :pray:
